reflection.text:
Unblinded compound is nocodazole (PubChem CID 4122, ChEMBL CHEMBL9514, e16/e17), identity checked as name and BBBC021 structure agree. Verdict approve was correct: agent MoA Microtubule destabilizers p=0.84 e15 matches truth MoA Microtubule destabilizers.

What the evidence got right:
- Quantitative morphology was decisive and dose-consistent. Wells w_1db1c2db0e 0.1 uM (nuc_solidity z=-24.2, act_mean z=+23.7, act_tub_ratio z=+20.1, e2), w_0fd9e97372 1 uM (act_tub_ratio z=+32.3, nuc_solidity z=-30.4, nuc_form_factor z=-24.2, e3), w_ded8987f6d 0.03 uM (tub_glcm_contrast z=+22.4, nuc_solidity z=-21.6, e7), and w_99b0bb31f5 3 uM (act_tub_ratio z=+43.4, nuc_solidity z=-20.3, e8) all showed extreme tubulin-related texture/ratio changes plus nuclear irregularity.
- Atlas comparison was robust: NSC vote 2/2 and 10/10 k-neighbours at 2 wells (e4), remaining 3/4 NSC and 10/10 k-neighbours at 4 wells (e9). This outweighed subjective calls.
- Dose-response synthesis was the tie-breaker: tub_mean Spearman rho=-1.00 p=0 over 4 wells/4 doses (e12) directly supports net tubulin loss with increasing dose, the expected direction for a destabilizer. This justified the hypothesis update e14 ranking Microtubule destabilizers 0.84 vs stabilizers 0.09, Aurora 0.04, Actin disruptors 0.03, and the rationale in e15.
- Literature context is consistent with a destabilizer class defined by colchicine-site binding and depolymerization, as exemplified in the returned literature set PMID 28640209, and with coordination between microtubule stability and actin polymerization PMID 15897190, which helps interpret the act_mean increase without invoking a primary actin target. PubMed search for 'nocodazole microtubule destabilizer mechanism tubulin polymerization' returned 11 hits/5 returned (e18), while 'nocodazole multinucleation actin cytoskeleton phenotype MCF-7' returned 0 hits (e19), indicating no direct curated hit in this run to explain the actin upregulation specifically.

What misled or was ambiguous and why:
- Microscopist describe_phenotype on 2 fields each gave conflicting, low-observation candidates: Actin disruptors (6 observations, e5) and Aurora kinase inhibitors (4 observations, e6), both noting only 'density lower vs DMSO'. These visual assessments lack quantitation and were correctly down-weighted relative to e4/e9.
- Single-well features could mimic other MoAs: e7 tub_glcm_contrast z=+22.4 was used in hypothesis history to support Microtubule stabilizers 0.09, and the very high act_mean z=+19.5 to +23.7 across e2/e7/e8 and act_tub_ratio z=+20.1 to +43.4 could be read as actin disruption. In context of e12 tub loss, this is better interpreted as relative actin increase after microtubule depolymerization rather than primary actin disruption; no independent actin dose trend supported it (act_mean rho=-0.60 p=0.4, e10, n=4 wells, underpowered).
- Nuclear changes (nuc_solidity -21.6 to -30.4, nuc_form_factor -24.2) mimic Aurora polyploidy, but dose_response for frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.60 p=0.4 (e11) was not significant on only 4 wells, and frac_mitotic_like was constant across acquired wells (e13), so no mitotic-arrest signature was captured to support Aurora.

Acquisition choices:
- Strategy was to sample mid dose (0.1 uM, e2) then high dose (1 uM, e3) to get atlas vote early, then fill low-mid 0.03 uM (e7) and top 3 uM (e8) to test Aurora vs microtubule emergence. This left 4 of 8 wells unused per e1 (doses 0.001-3 uM, 4/4 wells left initially), so lowest doses 0.001-0.01 uM were never sampled. That was sufficient for the destabilizer call but meant we could not test a transient mitotic arrest peak or threshold effect at low dose, and dose_response tests were limited to n=4 with p=0.4 for e10/e11.
- Reliance on act_tub_ratio as top z-score is sensitive to denominator (tubulin) loss; without independent tub immunofluorescence quantitation in the same field, ratio inflation is ambiguous. The decisive measurement was the monotonic tub_mean decrease e12, not the ratio.

Missed/limitations: ChEMBL lookup returned 'none curated' mechanisms (e16/e17), so we depended entirely on phenotypic atlas and internal dose trend. Literature search did not return a direct nocodazole-specific mechanistic paper in this run despite 11 hits, so conclusion rested on phenotypic similarity, not on literature confirmation of nocodazole binding site in this dataset. Next experiment proposed - live-cell tubulin polymerization + phospho-H3 and washout regrowth vs vincristine/taxol controls - remains needed to formally distinguish destabilization from stabilization.

This reflection is based solely on cell-line screening morphology and should not be interpreted as clinical guidance.
what_was_right: Atlas NSC 3/4 and 10/10 k-neighbours (e9) plus early 2/2 vote (e4) correctly identified microtubule destabilizers across 0.03-3 uM
